decisions.reason: F2 is false for negative roots (w=e, gamma=-alpha). Added gamma in Phi+; step 1.1 already chooses gamma positive, and the converse uses beta positive. Reflection conjugation, reduced-root uniqueness and the saturated-chain length argument prove the unchanged statement. No conclusion relied on the false negative-root extension.

The cited supplier actually proves monotonicity: def-bruhat-order-on-a-finite-weyl-group Proof 2.1 checks all four ascent/descent cases on a saturated edge; Proof 3.1 concatenates them along chains, and 5.1 identifies that order with Bruhat order. F1 accurately says the same item proves this. The rank-two proof uses this proved consequence only for two ascents in 2.1(c), then reduces the both-descent case to length(x)-1; its two subcases count respectively one rising middle plus xs, or two rising middles. The minimal length-two case is covered by 2.2. No unsupported mathematical premise remains.

F5 wrongly included negative roots; beta=-alpha and u=s_alpha contradict it. Restored beta in Phi+ and explicitly chose the positive representative of every reflection in F6 and step 1.2. The reduced-word induction pairs with the positive simple root; in each Bruhat descent, v_j inverse alpha_j is the negative of v_(j-1) inverse alpha_j and hence positive. Thus the arbitrary-positive-root embedding theorem applies at every step. One-dimensional Hom spaces and the universal property give unique singular-vector images and nested submodules. Removed the unused AC-dependent iff homomorphism criterion: the constructive embeddings prove the required forward implication without it. Statement is unchanged.

F1 attributed a simultaneous normalization to a supplier whose interface establishes nested images and one-dimensional Hom spaces. Proportionality alone cannot prove equality of abstract maps: scaling one diamond edge scales only one composite. Replaced that imported normalization by a local construction: fix j_w into M(lambda), j_e=id, and define iota_(u,v)=j_v inverse j_u for every comparable pair. Nested images make it well-defined, and j_y times either diamond composite equals j_x; injectivity of j_y proves equality. The final step proves all comparable triple compositions agree and explicitly records the dependence of abstract-copy normalization on j_w. The literal canonical-submodule inclusions and original Statement remain unchanged.

The typed-cut Statement supplies filtration types, not exactness on all O-objects. Added thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character as the exact F3 prerequisite and direct dependency. Its Statement asserts exact projections, and its Proof 2.1 verifies surjectivity by lifting a character-component vector and taking the matching component of the lift. Thus projection preserves the tensored resolution; scalar central action fixes its final term. The type calculation is sound: a surviving pair gives u inverse nu=lambda+sum Pi_(u inverse w), whereas every finite-dimensional weight is below lambda; pointedness forces the sum empty, u=w and nu=w lambda. Extremal multiplicity one and regularity yield the stated type, including lambda=0 and rank zero. Statement unchanged; no new lemma is needed.

The old title said onto the kernel, exceeding the injectivity-only Statement and proof. Corrected the title to an injection into kernel coinvariants. PBW identifies one distinct-weight coinvariant generator per degree-(k+1) summand; every such generator has a nonzero differential component along a simple descent. Square-zero puts that image in ker d_k. The kernel-factor supplier proves its length bound by comparing finite Jordan-Holder multisets with the weak resolution, and the highest-weight-survival supplier proves nonvanishing modulo n-minus by finite-length induction. Its hypotheses apply with threshold k+1, so distinct-weight images are independent. For an empty next layer the zero domain is injective. No surjectivity is asserted or proved here; the page correctly reserves it for the later dimension count. Statement and proof unchanged.
